content: Montgomery Regional Hospital (MRH) is located in the town of Blacksburg, within Montgomery County, Virginia. It operates as a subsidiary of the Hospital Corporation of America (HCA). The hospital is certified as a Level III trauma center, indicating its capability to provide prompt assessment, resuscitation, surgery, intensive care, and stabilization of injured patients, as well as emergency operations. Montgomery Regional Hospital was established in 1971. On August 20, 2006, a tragic incident occurred at MRH. William Morva, who had been incarcerated and awaiting trial for an attempted robbery charge, was brought to the hospital after sustaining a sprained ankle and wrist while in jail. While at the hospital, he requested to use the restroom. During this time, he attacked and fatally shot Derrick McFarland, a security guard in the emergency department. He also attacked a Montgomery County sheriff's deputy. Morva managed to escape from the emergency department but was apprehended the following day. During his escape, on the morning of August 21, he shot and killed Montgomery County Sheriff's Corporal Eric Sutphin. On April 16, 2007, during the Virginia Tech massacre, Montgomery Regional Hospital received and treated several patients who had sustained injuries during the tragic event.
